title: Yu Xiang–Style Sweet Garlic Sauce
description: A generous measure of garlic, smooth red pepper and rice vinegar gives this mild Sichuan-inspired sauce a sweet, tangy edge.
equipment: Vitamix or immersion blender with tall heatproof jug

ingredients.name: fresh garlic cloves
ingredients.note: Peel and finely grate unless the step specifies otherwise.

ingredients.name: fresh ginger juice
ingredients.note: Finely grate peeled ginger and squeeze out the juice.

ingredients.name: peeled roasted red bell pepper
ingredients.note: Plain home-roasted pepper with skin and seeds removed.

ingredients.name: mild white miso
ingredients.note: Use plain white miso, ideally no more than 215 mg sodium per teaspoon. Low-sodium batch: use 1/4 tsp total.

ingredients.name: coconut aminos
ingredients.note: Use Coconut Secret Original at 90 mg sodium per teaspoon. Low-sodium batch: use 1 tsp total.

ingredients.name: low-sodium mushroom broth
ingredients.note: For a plain infusion, steep sliced mushrooms in hot water, strain and add no salt. Estimate assumes 15 mg sodium per cup.

ingredients.name: mild ground gochugaru
ingredients.note: Choose unsalted mild Korean red pepper, finely ground.

steps.title: Soften the garlic
steps.text: Warm {oil} and cook {ga}, {gi} and {go} at low heat for 1–2 minutes, keeping the garlic pale.

steps.title: Join the two bases
steps.text: Stir the red pepper puree into the garlic and simmer for 4 minutes. The softened pepper and mild miso give the sauce body and gentle warmth.

steps.title: Mix the slurry
steps.text: Stir {sl} into {cw} in a small cup until smooth.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Whisk the slurry into the gently simmering base. Cook for 60–90 seconds, stirring, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Check the yield
steps.text: Measure the sauce in a heatproof cup. Aim for 1 cup. If short, loosen with a little hot sodium-free water. If over, return it to the pan and simmer briefly to the mark.

steps.title: Serve the sauce
steps.text: Spoon over soft braised eggplant or sliced pork. Stir a little extra chile into individual portions.

notes: Yield: 1 cup, or four 1/4-cup portions. Low-sodium option for the full batch: Use 1 tsp coconut aminos in place of 4 tsp. Use 1/4 tsp mild white miso in place of 1/2 tsp. Use the same final 1-cup yield and 1/4-cup serving. Make ahead: Make the sauce the day before and portion it before chilling. Refrigerate in shallow covered portions within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze flat in 1/4-cup portions for up to 2 months. Whisk again after thawing to restore the texture. Fridge reheat: Reheat a portion in a small pan, stirring to a brief boil and at least 165°F. Loosen with a splash of water if it tightens. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator, then use the fridge reheat method. Option A uses the listed seasonings. For a gentler Option B, skip the gochugaru, halve the garlic and use 1 teaspoon rice vinegar. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/4 of recipe): 45 kcal, 0.6 g protein, 7.8 g total carbohydrate, 1.3 g fat, 0.3 g fiber, 121 mg sodium. Low-sodium version per 1/4 cup: 40 kcal, 0.5 g protein, 6.7 g total carbohydrate, 1.2 g fat, 0.3 g fiber, 40 mg sodium. Figures cover the sauce alone. Sodium varies with brands.
